answer: Noise token injection at the vine: each block hash seeds a pseudo-random token that only registered agents may claim. Basalt hardness ensures the hash cannot be ground cheaply, since each trial costs one full hash and rejects most outcomes. On the tundra of cheap identities, a farmer must split stake across many wallets, so claimed noise scales linearly while registration bond scales quadratically. Break-even arrives when gas plus bond per identity exceeds the expected noise reward, roughly nine wallets at current difficulty. It works because honest miners claim noise once per verified.
